title: Elastic mini-lane rotation and scope accordion for mid-cycle surge
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Problem: During the last two cycles we hit concentrated demand spikes in a narrow set of initiatives (runtime and dedicated onboarding) that starved cross-team float and caused rushed scope cuts. Objective: Create an operational pattern — the 'mini-lane rotation' combined with a 'scope accordion' — that lets PMs reallocate small specialist capacity for 1-2 sprint windows while maintaining predictable commitments and clear criteria for temporary scope compression and re-expansion.
acceptance_criteria: A concise playbook doc is published in Confluence with step-by-step runway checks and decision gates
Three pilot rotations executed in the next cycle with post-mortem and metrics (time-to-rotate, blocked work, scope re-expansion rate)
Dashboards updated to show lane-level committed vs floating FTE and predicted burnout risk
Stakeholders sign off on rollback and priority reversion rules
plan: Week 1: Draft playbook and run a tabletop with Eng leads, Design lead, and SRE to validate guardrails (latency/SLOs, oncall load)
Week 2: Implement two lightweight dashboard panels (lane capacity, surge eligibility) with product analytics team; create a templated Slack rotation announcement and escalation path
Week 3: Pilot with one micro-lane (infra-tooling) to rotate two engineers for a 7-day surge; use a scoped scope-accordion to compress noncritical stories by 20%
Week 4: Collect metrics, hold retro, refine thresholds and document decision checklist for future cycles
risks: Cross-team friction if rotation removes critical subject matter expertise (mitigation: must meet eligibility checklist)
Hidden dependencies cause slowdowns in receiving teams (mitigation: pre-rotation dependency sweep and explicit handover notes)
Overuse of mini-lanes could erode long-term feature velocity (mitigation: limit to two rotations per team per quarter)
Insufficient monitoring on scope re-expansion could leave technical debt unaddressed (mitigation: track deferred story backlog and schedule re-fill windows)
stakeholders: Engineering leads: Marcus Feldman, Priya Kapoor
